description: Real pulls of five catalogued agent images, a running container from one of them, and near-miss tags an exact route must decline.
why: The only scenario that asserts container identifiers against live registries, and the reason the catalog carries no fixture-backed image. `deep: true` is what makes it possible: containers.sql is `expensive`, so it is absent from dist/discovery-linux.sql and this scenario asserts against `bin/discover --deep` instead -- the same artifact and the same bounded runner that ship. It now covers all three container routes at once. `images` is the tag anyone can set. `image_labels` is the vendor-set OCI `source`, which is why the two URLs are in must_contain: they prove the label branch emits and that the current OpenHands and goose images really do carry them. `container_images` needs a RUNNING container, because docker_containers lists running ones only -- an image pull can never exercise it. The controls are the half that makes it a test: `paulgauthier/aider-fork` has a catalogued value as a PREFIX, so declining it proves the routes compare whole repository names and not substrings, and it is run as a container too so that proof covers the container route rather than only the image one. `correctly declined` and `never looked at` are the same shape without forbid_evidence.
known_gaps: A pull proves the registry still serves this repository under this name. It does not prove the image is the vendor's: an image name is chosen by whoever tags it, so `docker tag alpine paulgauthier/aider` produces the same finding. The `image_labels` route is the answer to that for the agents whose vendors set labels, and aider and swe-agent are exactly the ones who do not -- so for those two the finding remains as forgeable as the tag.

The container probe runs `sleep`, not the agent. It proves the daemon reports a running container from a catalogued image and that the route matches it; it proves nothing about an agent actually working, which would need credentials and a model endpoint this scenario deliberately does not hold.

Nothing here reads processes inside the container. docker_container_processes requires a constraint on the container id and can be reached through a join, but the cmdline it returns can carry an API key, so it is not collected until redaction is designed.
swe-agent's `latest` tag was built 2024-12-07, twenty-one months before this scenario was written. The pull proves the registry still serves it; it does not prove anyone still publishes there.
